📊 Crypto Midweek: Election Jitters Meet a Fragile Rebound

Markets: Bitcoin rose 0.7% to $78,354 and Ether gained 1.4% to $2,323 after recovering from overnight losses, Reuters reported. The broader crypto market has shed about $300B over the past month amid higher borrowing costs and concerns about risk appetite.

Policy & security: Democrats’ midterm wins put the outlook for U.S. crypto legislation in focus. Separately, Binance customers withdrew a net $4.72B after the exchange reopened following last week’s $6B hack, Reuters reported.

Sources: Reuters · Market data

📊 Crypto Brief: Bitcoin Rebounds Above $80K After Midterm Selloff

U.S. policy: Bitcoin bounced after Democrats secured both chambers of Congress, but the result may complicate the crypto industry’s push for federal market-structure rules. Reuters reported that crypto-backed PACs lost several high-profile races, including Ohio’s Senate contest, despite heavy spending.

Market & DeFi: CoinDesk’s market ticker showed BTC at $80,503 (+3.8%) and ETH at $2,436 (+6.1%). Its DeFi Select index gained about 5%, with all seven constituents higher; broader sentiment remained cautious, with the Fear & Greed Index at 37.
